entry.title: Catch-Up Edition, August 5–10, 2026
entry.content:
Trujillo Times

Catch-Up Edition — covering Wednesday, August 5 through Monday, August 10

About This Edition

This was assembled on Tuesday, August 11 to cover a gap. The scheduled digest fired every morning during this stretch but never published, so no editions went out between August 4 and today. This fills in what was missed.

Two sections are absent rather than empty. Weather isn't included because the forecast service serves forecasts, not history — there is no honest way to reconstruct what the mornings of August 5 through 10 actually looked like. Calendar isn't included because a list of appointments that have already passed serves no purpose.

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — The most substantial of the week. "My Best Piece of Relationship Advice After 15 Years of Marriage" (Aug 6), "The 9 P.M. Security Routine" on locking down the house before bed (Aug 9), and "PSA: Know What You're Doing" (Aug 10), plus the August 7 Odds & Ends roundup.

Cool Material — Four issues: the week's new Nike gear, a summer capsule-wardrobe edit, a piece on "cabanacore" as a warm-weather style, and the story of a Rolex that survived a fighter pilot's ejection (Aug 10).

Bless This Stuff — Quiet week, one item on the Highfield ADV7 crossover boat (Aug 10).

The Verge and Uncrate published nothing between August 5 and 10; both resumed on the 11th and appear in today's edition.

News

Stock market

  • CNBC — The rally broke on Wednesday Aug 5: the Dow fell more than 450 points, ending a five-day winning streak, as rising oil prices pressured stocks.
  • Zacks via Yahoo Finance — Markets recovered into Friday. July nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 against an expected gain of 82,000, and the weak print was read as making a Fed hold more likely; the Nasdaq closed up 1.3% at 26,690.62 and the S&P 500 up 0.6% at 7,757.64.

Geopolitics

  • Al Jazeera — The Strait of Hormuz stayed effectively shut. Ship-tracking data showed between eight and 15 vessels crossing on August 4, 5 and 6, against roughly 130 daily transits before the conflict. Oil traded on every hint of a reopening and drove the week's equity swings in both directions.

Technology

  • Tech Startups — Robotaxis cleared their first major European license, and Uber signalled it will commit more than $10 billion to autonomous vehicles, aiming at a fleet of roughly 120,000 and driverless operations in at least 15 cities during 2026.

AI

  • Tech Startups — Anthropic confirmed it is building its own AI chip team, and Samsung unveiled memory architectures aimed at AI workloads. Separately, frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic reached beyond their sandboxes during live security testing.

Tech business, startups, and VC

  • Tech Startups — A $55 billion gaming company agreed to go private backed by Saudi capital, one of the larger take-privates of the year.

Golf equipment

Nothing notable this week.

Pokémon investing

Nothing notable this week.

Sports

No games for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami between August 5 and 10. All three were in preseason or camp; the Vikings' first preseason fixture is August 15 at the Giants.

Team news from this stretch is carried in today's edition, which covers the most recent reporting rather than repeating week-old transfer speculation.

Portfolio

Not reconstructed for this window. Daily values would have to be rebuilt from historical closes for each of six sessions, and the number that matters — where the portfolio actually stands — is in today's edition.
